clue.text: Reformed tart is game to see JP

indicators.note: something reformed has been made over into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A reformed tart who is game for anything goes to see a magistrate.
explanation.definitionFit: A JP, or Justice of the Peace, is a lay judicial officer sitting in a lower court.

clue.text: Finance allows Kitty to have bread

parts.note: a kitty is a pool of money, also called the bank in gambling
a roll is a small loaf of bread

explanation.surface: Someone's finances let the cat be fed with bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitty' looks like a pet but is the pot of money.
explanation.definitionFit: To bankroll is to fund or finance a venture, a verb sense of supplying the money.

clue.text: Enthusiast to count: it includes one hundred

parts.note: to count up is to add

indicators.note: includes means the word it holds the next piece within it

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for one hundred

explanation.surface: A fan has to count, and the total includes a hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: An addict, in the loose sense, is a devotee or fan of some pursuit, like a jazz addict.

clue.text: Shooting party members got up to get warm

indicators.note: in a down clue, got up means the word is read from the bottom upward, reversed

parts.note: on a shoot, the people with guns are themselves called guns

explanation.surface: Members of a shooting party stand up to get warm.
explanation.definitionFit: Snug means cosily warm and sheltered, as in a snug bed.

clue.text: Incline to keep unemployment benefit for a teenager

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: an ascent is an upward slope or incline
the dole is the British informal name for unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: A slope must hold back jobless money meant for a teenager.
explanation.definitionFit: An adolescent is a young person between childhood and adulthood, so a teenager.

clue.text: Soccer boot twisted in dive

indicators.note: in means the twisted letters go inside the word for dive

parts.note: a dive is a sudden fall, as when a player tumbles

indicators.note: twisted says the letters of boot are bent out of their order

explanation.surface: A footballer's boot twists as he takes a dive.
explanation.definitionFit: Soccer is the other name for association football, the game played with a round ball.

clue.text: Type of paste used by salmon daily

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sort of paste is used every day on salmon.
explanation.definitionFit: Almond paste, or marzipan, is a confection made from ground almonds and sugar.

clue.text: Mother's mother nearly gets donation

indicators.note: nearly means the word is not quite complete, losing its last letter

parts.note: a grant is a sum of money given, a donation

explanation.surface: Grandmother almost gets a gift of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Gran is the familiar word for a grandmother, a parent's mother.

clue.text: Left Group One to feature in commercial

indicators.note: to feature in something is to appear inside it, so these pieces sit within the other

parts.note: an ad is a commercial or advertisement
a band is a musical group
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pop group was left out of the line-up for a TV commercial.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoned means left behind or deserted, in the past-participle sense of left.

clue.text: One who looks lecherously breaks leg in Oregon

indicators.note: in means the broken letters sit inside the abbreviation for Oregon

parts.note: OR is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Oregon

indicators.note: breaks means the letters of leg are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A lecher suffers a broken leg while in Oregon.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogler is someone who stares at others with obvious desire, a leering watcher.

clue.text: One not known to Heather provides a hint

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
NK is the abbreviation for not known
ling is another name for common heather

explanation.surface: Someone a girl called Heather has never met offers a clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name but is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkling is a slight suspicion or vague notion, a faint hint of something.

clue.text: Like a lengthened skirt, it's a disappointment

definitions.meaning: a skirt lengthened by releasing its hem has had that hem lowered
a failure to meet expectations, an anticlimax

explanation.surface: A lengthened skirt turns out to be a disappointment.
explanation.definitionFit: A hem let down makes a skirt longer, and a letdown is also a disappointing outcome.

clue.text: Fish to sell, recipe included

indicators.note: included means the letter is placed inside the word for selling

parts.note: to tout is to sell, especially pushily
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin recipe, take

explanation.surface: A fishmonger sells fish with a recipe thrown in.
explanation.definitionFit: Trout is a freshwater fish of the salmon family.

clue.text: Bad sentry failing as a witness

indicators.note: failing suggests the letters collapse out of order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A bad sentry, failing in his duty, can only stand by as a witness.
explanation.definitionFit: A bystander is someone present but not involved, who sees an event as a witness.

clue.text: Love letter found with tie in dull box

indicators.note: to found metal is to melt and cast it anew, so these letters are recast

explanation.surface: A love letter turns up with a tie in a dull box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' looks like 'discovered' but means cast afresh, reshaping TIE and DULLBOX.
explanation.definitionFit: A billet-doux is a love letter, from the French for sweet note.

clue.text: Actual sound recorded twice running on sort of tape machine

indicators.note: a recorded sound is heard, so the word is taken by how it is said

parts.note: actual means real
running on to the next thing, as in moving to it

indicators.note: twice means the sounded word is used a second time

parts.note: actual means real, used again

explanation.surface: Real sound is recorded twice in succession on a tape deck.
explanation.walkthrough: REAL said aloud gives REEL, which appears twice either side of TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel-to-reel machine plays open spools of magnetic tape, a type of tape recorder.

clue.text: He will free everyone first, causing pandemonium

indicators.note: first places the word for everyone at the front of the answer

parts.note: all means everyone
he will contracts to he'll
to let loose is to set free

explanation.surface: A liberator will free everybody, causing chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: All hell let loose is an idiom for a scene of chaos and uproar.

clue.text: Elgar composed differently in the finale, when amplified

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters go inside the word for finale

parts.note: the finale is the end

indicators.note: composed differently means the letters of the composer's name are rearranged

explanation.surface: Elgar's finale was rewritten in a bigger arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' suggests music by Elgar, but with 'differently' it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlarged means made bigger, and amplified likewise means increased in size or volume.

clue.text: Near to getting praise by instalments

parts.note: on can mean close to or near, as in a town on the coast
credit is praise or acknowledgement

explanation.surface: Someone is close to getting praise, bit by bit.
explanation.definitionFit: Buying on credit means paying later, usually in instalments.

clue.text: Better time for cutting down on food of high quality

parts.note: to better is to surpass, to excel

parts.words: time for cutting down on food
parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: A better diet season gives food of top quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like an adjective but is the verb to surpass.
explanation.definitionFit: Excellent means outstanding, of very high quality.

clue.text: Safekeeping for a warhorse without a tail

indicators.note: without a tail means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a charger is a horse ridden into battle

explanation.surface: Someone takes custody of a warhorse that has lost its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Charge means care or custody, as in a child left in someone's charge.

clue.text: Rough, but not censored

definitions.meaning: of a gem, not yet shaped or polished
of a film, shown in full with no cuts

explanation.surface: Rough-edged but uncensored.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncut diamond is rough, and an uncut film has not been censored.

clue.text: Hesitant superior takes on new nurse

parts.note: U stands for upper class, socially superior

indicators.note: new means the letters of nurse are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A nervous senior takes on a new nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old British label for upper-class usage; 'new' turns NURSE into NSURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsure means doubtful, so hesitant about deciding.

clue.text: Traitors turning to wine marked "special"

indicators.note: turning means the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: rats are informers or traitors
red is red wine

explanation.surface: Traitors turn to wine labelled special.
explanation.definitionFit: A starred item is marked with an asterisk, flagging it as special or notable.

clue.text: Cupid got up and, they say, saw red

indicators.note: in a down clue, got up means the word is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love, the counterpart of Roman Cupid

explanation.surface: Cupid rose and, people say, lost his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they say, saw' is a second route: said in a British accent, saw sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sore skin is inflamed and red, as with a sore throat.

clue.text: Erasmus used one who, reportedly, needs bodies

indicators.note: used suggests the name is worked over and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Erasmus hired a man who needs bodies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' said aloud is kneads, what a masseur does to bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseur kneads the body with his hands, so he kneads bodies.

clue.text: It's the fashion for a maiden to be attracted to poetry

parts.note: M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: Being drawn to poetry is in fashion for a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A mode is a prevailing style or fashion, as in the latest mode.

clue.text: Scoundrel with an Irish accent first found missing

indicators.note: first found missing means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a brogue is a strong regional accent, especially an Irish one

explanation.surface: A scoundrel with an Irish accent was first to be found missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest rascal, a scoundrel.

clue.text: Mark subordinate to policy

parts.note: under means beneath in rank, subordinate to
a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: A junior marks the company policy.
explanation.definitionFit: To underline is to mark with a line beneath, emphasising it.
